newsitem.title: LATVIA: New Latvia government sets inflation, budget aims.
newsitem.headline: New Latvia government sets inflation, budget aims.

text.p: The new government of the Baltic state of Latvia on Wednesday issued its programme for the next year, aiming at a maximum inflation rate of nine percent for this year and seven percent in 1998.
The inflation targets are expected easily to be met as year-on-year inflation in June was just 7.5 percent.

The government programme also said it would aim at a balanced budget although the finance ministry has said that tax collection is below target this year, leading to a possible deficit of 10 million to 12 million lats.
The government declaration said the new administration would allow a fiscal deficit of 0.9 percent of GDP this year and 0.5 percent next year.
It said the deficit may be allowed to rise to one percent of GDP for spending for the state investment programme.
The new government is to be led by former economy minister Guntar Krasts, nominated for prime minister by the country's leading political parties.
A parliament vote of confidence to confirm the government in office is expected on August 7.
Former prime minister Andris Shkele was forced to resign after rows with the coalition parties.
The declaration also pledges to speed privatisation and complete it by July 1 of next year and to issue medium-term state Treasury bills next year.
It also aims to restructure Latvian Railways along market economy lines and increase the minimum wage by 10 percent in 1998.
